chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri reported to me, saying: Umar ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Bajali reported to us, saying: Hameed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Tasnim al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuaim al-Fadhl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Muqatil ibn Sulaiman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Abbas, who said:
I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:
"The foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In the gardens of bliss." (56:10-12)
He said: Jibreel told me: "That refers to Ali and his followers (Shi'a). They are the foremost towards Paradise, the ones brought near to God, Most High, by His honour bestowed upon them."

key_terms.السابقون: The foremost, those who take precedence in faith and good deeds
key_terms.المقربون: The ones brought near, those granted proximity to God
key_terms.شيعته: His followers/partisans (Shi'a), those who support and follow Ali

ai.seo_question: Who are "the foremost" (al-Sabiqun) mentioned in Quran 56:10-12 according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Mufid, Ibn Abbas reports that he asked the Prophet (SAWW) about the meaning of Quran 56:10-12 regarding "the foremost" who are "brought near" in gardens of bliss. The Prophet relayed that the angel Jibreel identified those described in these verses as Ali ibn Abi Talib and his followers (Shi'a), who will be the first to enter Paradise and the nearest to God through His special honour. This hadith reflects the early Muslim community's interest in understanding which figures the Quran's praise referred to.
